targetAudience.primary: Open-source toolchain, agent-runtime and capability-security engineers
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands repository configuration, child processes, environment variables and MCP helpers.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Repository-supplied executable configuration may legitimately run after workspace trust while still receiving unrelated ambient credentials from the launching process.

whyNow: Claude Code v2.1.238 release material documents folder-trust admission for project-controlled MCP helpers and separate removal of inherited credential environment variables for selected helper origins.

externalHook.description: Permission to execute repository-controlled code and permission to receive ambient secrets are separate grants with different blast radii.

coreProposition: Executable configuration should have separate capabilities for code execution and ambient secret or host-resource authority: workspace trust can authorize a repository-controlled helper to run without implicitly authorizing inherited credentials, while credential-environment filtering is a least-authority control rather than a sandbox.

originalValue.description: Separates origin-aware code admission from post-admission capability grants and turns explicit task context into a replacement for accidental parent-process authority.

readerTakeaway: Treat executable configuration as code, gate it by origin and trust, provide allowlisted task context, grant secrets separately, and require independent evidence for filesystem, network, process and external-effect isolation.

supported: Published v2.1.238 notes require folder trust for named project and agent-file MCP helper paths.
The same release notes state that selected project, plugin and agent-file headersHelper commands do not inherit credential environment variables.
Official documentation describes headersHelper as shell execution whose JSON output becomes connection headers.
Official documentation exposes purpose-specific helper variables.
unsupported: The exact credential-variable filter or regression-test matrix
Filesystem, network, process or credential-store sandboxing
Independent validation of the private implementation
uncertain: How the credential classification is maintained as providers change
How helpers declare and receive explicit capabilities beyond environment context

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general capability-security pattern for executable configuration and agent tooling without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The release and documentation provide a concrete two-control example, while the Research Object contributes a transferable post-admission capability model with clear evidence limits.
